title: Lattice-supported formal series as a module retract
statement:
Let $L$ be a commutative ring, $r\geq0$ an integer, $M\subseteq\mathbf Z^r$ an additive subgroup, and $Q=M\cap\mathbf N^r$. Put $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_r]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and
$$A_Q=\{F\in A:c_e(F)=0\text{ whenever }e\notin Q\}.$$
Then $A_Q$ is an $L$-subalgebra of $A$. The coefficient map
$$\pi:A\to A_Q,\qquad c_e(\pi F)=\begin{cases}c_e(F)&e\in Q,\\0&e\notin Q,\end{cases}$$
is additive, fixes $A_Q$ pointwise, and satisfies $\pi(ab)=a\pi(b)$ for all $a\in A_Q$ and $b\in A$. More generally, for every commutative $L$-algebra $R$ and injective $L$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi:R\to A$ with image exactly $A_Q$, there is a unique additive map $\rho:A\to R$ such that $\varphi(\rho(b))=\pi(b)$ for all $b\in A$ (viewing $A_Q$ inside $A$). It satisfies
$$\rho(\varphi(t)b)=t\rho(b)\quad(t\in R,\ b\in A),\qquad \rho\varphi=\operatorname{id}_R.$$
Thus $\rho$ is an $R$-linear retraction when $A$ is an $R$-module through $\varphi$. No completeness, locality or finite-generation hypothesis on $L$ or $Q$ is required.

proof.text: Since $M$ is a subgroup, $0\in Q$ and $u,v\in Q$ imply $u+v\in Q$. Moreover, for $u\in Q$ and $v\in\mathbf N^r$, one has $u+v\in Q$ if and only if $v\in Q$: the forward implication follows from $v=(u+v)-u\in M$, and the reverse from addition in $M$. All these vectors are nonnegative by hypothesis.

proof.text: Use the coefficientwise addition and finite convolution product of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Zero, sums and negatives of series supported on $Q$ remain supported there. Constants are supported at $0\in Q$. If $a,b\in A_Q$ and $e\notin Q$, each summand $c_u(a)c_v(b)$ with $u+v=e$ vanishes: if both $u,v$ belonged to $Q$, Step 1 would put $e$ in $Q$. Thus $ab\in A_Q$. These closure properties make $A_Q$ an $L$-subalgebra.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70 (PDF p.76), is motivation only. Auxiliary agent coefficient argument for the subgroup-supported retraction, refining old steps 8--9 of lem-trf-completed-monoid-support-projection.

proof.text: A series is a family of coefficients by [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], so the displayed coefficient rule defines $\pi F$ uniquely and gives an element of $A_Q$. For $e\in Q$ the rule preserves addition of coefficients; for $e\notin Q$ both sides have coefficient zero. Thus $\pi$ is additive. If $F\in A_Q$, the discarded coefficients already vanish, so $\pi F=F$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70 (PDF p.76), is motivation only. Auxiliary agent coefficient argument for the subgroup-supported retraction, refining old steps 8--9 of lem-trf-completed-monoid-support-projection.

proof.text:
Fix $a\in A_Q$, $b\in A$ and $e\in\mathbf N^r$. In the finite convolution formula of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], discard terms with $u\notin Q$ since $c_u(a)=0$. For every remaining pair $u+v=e$, Step 1 gives $e\in Q\iff v\in Q$. Consequently
$$c_e(\pi(ab))=\mathbf1_{e\in Q}\sum_{u+v=e}c_u(a)c_v(b)=\sum_{u+v=e}c_u(a)\mathbf1_{v\in Q}c_v(b)=c_e(a\pi(b)).$$
Here each indicator is $1$ or $0$ in $L$. Equality of coefficient families proves $\pi(ab)=a\pi(b)$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70 (PDF p.76), is motivation only. Auxiliary agent coefficient argument for the subgroup-supported retraction, refining old steps 8--9 of lem-trf-completed-monoid-support-projection.

proof.text:
For each $b\in A$, the image hypothesis and $\pi(b)\in A_Q$ give an $x\in R$ with $\varphi(x)=\pi(b)$; injectivity makes $x$ unique. Define $\rho(b)=x$. Additivity of $\pi$ gives $\varphi(\rho(b+b'))=\varphi(\rho(b)+\rho(b'))$, hence additivity of $\rho$. Step 4 and multiplicativity of $\varphi$ give
$$\varphi(\rho(\varphi(t)b))=\pi(\varphi(t)b)=\varphi(t)\pi(b)=\varphi(t\rho(b)).$$
Injectivity yields $\rho(\varphi(t)b)=t\rho(b)$. Also $\varphi(\rho(\varphi(t)))=\pi(\varphi(t))=\varphi(t)$ by Step 3, so $\rho\varphi=\operatorname{id}_R$. Any other map satisfying the displayed defining equation agrees pointwise by injectivity. For the action $t\cdot b=\varphi(t)b$, additivity and the scalar identity are exactly $R$-linearity. Only finite sums and subgroup subtraction were used; no topological or finiteness assumptions are needed.

lean.statement: theorem lattice_support_coefficient_retraction (L : Type u) [CommRing L] (r : ℕ) (M : AddSubgroup (Fin r → ℤ)) : ∃ S : Subalgebra L (MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L), (∀ F : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L, F ∈ S ↔ ∀ e : Fin r →₀ ℕ, (fun i ↦ (e i : ℤ)) ∉ M → coeff e F = 0) ∧ ∃ π : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L →+ S, (∀ (F : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L) (e : Fin r →₀ ℕ), (((fun i ↦ (e i : ℤ)) ∈ M → coeff e (π F : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L) = coeff e F) ∧ ((fun i ↦ (e i : ℤ)) ∉ M → coeff e (π F : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L) = 0))) ∧ (∀ a : S, π (a : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L) = a) ∧ (∀ (a : S) (b : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L), π ((a : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L) * b) = a * π b) ∧ ∀ (R : Type v) [CommRing R] [Algebra L R] (φ : R →ₐ[L] MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L), Function.Injective φ → Set.range φ = (S : Set (MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L)) → ∃ ρ : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L →+ R, (∀ b : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L, φ (ρ b) = (π b : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L)) ∧ (∀ (t : R) (b : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L), ρ (φ t * b) = t * ρ b) ∧ (∀ t : R, ρ (φ t) = t) ∧ ∀ ρ' : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L →+ R, (∀ b : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L, φ (ρ' b) = (π b : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) L)) → ρ' = ρ
